questions.q: Two metal strips are riveted together at their ends by four rivets, each of diameter $6\text{mm}$. Assuming that each of the rivets carries one-quarter of the load, the maximum tension that can be produced in the riveted strip is [Breaking shear stress of the rivet = $6.9 \times {10}^{7}Pa$]
questions.solution:
Diameter of each rivet $( \text{D} ) = 6\text{mm}$

$∴ \text{Radius (r)} = \dfrac{\text{D}}{2} = \text{3 mm} = 3 \times {10}^{- 3} \text{m}$

Maximum shearing stress on each rivet = 6.9 × 10^{7} Pa

Let w be the maximum load that can be subjected to the riveted strip.
As each rivet carry one-quarter of the load, therefore

$\text{Load on each rivet} = \dfrac{\text{w}}{4}$

$\text{Maximum shearing stress} = \dfrac{\text{Maximum shearing force}}{\text{Area}}$

$∴ \text{6.9} \times {10}^{7} = \dfrac{\text{w / 4}}{\text{\pi} r^{2}}$

or $\text{w} = 6.9 \times {10}^{7} 4{\text{\pi r}^{2}$

or $\text{w} = 6.9 \times {10}^{7} \times 4 \times 3.14 \times {( 3 \times {10}^{- 3} )}^{2}$

$= 6.9 \times 4 \times 3.14 \times 9 \times 10$

$= 7.8 \times {10}^{3} \text{N}$

questions.q: A solid sphere made out of metal having a bulk modulus of $2 \times {10}^{11}{Nm}^{- 2}$ is charged uniformly to a surface charge density $\sigma = \sqrt{\alpha{ε}_{0}}{Cm}^{- 2}$, where ${ε}_{0}$ is the permittivity of free space and $\alpha$ (magnitude = $1$) is a positive constant of appropriate dimensions. If the volume strain produced in the sphere after charging is $x \times {10}^{- 11}$, then the value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
Bulk modulus is given by

$B = \dfrac{- \DeltaP}{\dfrac{\DeltaV}{V}}$

The outward electrostatic pressure is

${P}_{electrostatic} = \dfrac{{\sigma}^{2}}{2{ε}_{0}} = - \DeltaP$

$⇒ \dfrac{\DeltaV}{V} = \dfrac{\dfrac{{\sigma}^{2}}{2{ε}_{0}}}{B}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\DeltaV}{V} = \dfrac{\dfrac{{\left(\sqrt{\alpha{ε}_{0}}\right)}^{2}}{2{ε}_{0}}}{2 \times {10}^{11}} = 0 . 25 \times {10}^{- 11}$

questions.q: A cube of aluminium of side $6cm$ is subjected to a tangential force such that the top face is shears through $0.012\text{cm}$ relative to the bottom face. The tangential force is $k \times {10}^{10}dyne$. What is the value of $k$? [Shear modulus of the material is $η = 2 \times {10}^{11}dyne{cm}^{- 2}$]
questions.solution:
Lateral displacement, $x = 0 . 012cm$

$∴$ Shearing strain,

$\theta = \dfrac{x}{L} = \dfrac{0 . 012}{6} = 0 . 002$

Shearing stress, $\dfrac{F}{a} = η\theta$

$= 2 \times {10}^{11} \times 0 . 002$

$= 4 \times {10}^{8}{dynecm}^{- 2}$

Shearing force, $F =$ shearing stress $\times$ area

$= 4 \times {10}^{8} \times ( L{)}^{2}$

$= 4 \times {10}^{8} \times ( 6{)}^{2}$

$= 1 . 44 \times {10}^{10}dyne$

$⇒ K = 1 . 44$

questions.q: A stone of mass $1 . 3kg$ is being rotated in a horizontal plane as a conical pendulum with the help of a $140cm$ long aluminium wire of cross-sectional area $1{mm}^{2}$. The wire makes an angle $\theta = 75 °$ with the vertical. What is the increment in the length (in $mm$) of the wire? [Young's modulus of aluminium ${Y}_{Al} = 7 \times {10}^{10}{\text{N m}}^{\text{-2}}$, $sin75 ° \approx 0 . 97$, $cos75 ° \approx 0 . 26$, $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$]
questions.solution:
The figure below shows the stone being rotated as a conical pendulum such that the wire makes an angle of $75 °$ with the vertical. Let us assume that the radius $OA$ of the circle is equal to $r$

For vertical equilibrium of the stone

$Tcos75 ° = Mg$

$T = \dfrac{Mg}{cos75 °}$

The elongation in the wire is

$∆ L = \dfrac{TL}{AY} = \dfrac{MgL}{AYcos75 °}$

$⇒ ∆ L = \dfrac{1 . 3 \times 10 \times 1 . 4}{{10}^{- 6} \times 7 \times {10}^{10} \times 0 . 26} = {10}^{- 3}m = 1mm$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform rod of length $l$ is acted upon by a force $F$ in a gravity-free region, as shown in the figure. If the area of cross-section of the rod is $A$ and it's Young's modulus is $Y$, then the elastic potential energy stored in the rod due to& elongation is
questions.solution:
The acceleration of the rod is

$a = \dfrac{F}{m}$

So, the tension in the rod at a distance $x$ from the free end is

$T\left(x\right) = \dfrac{mx}{l} \times \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{Fx}{l}$

The longitudinal stress developed inside the rod at a distance $x$ from the free end is

$\sigma = \dfrac{T\left(x\right)}{A} = \dfrac{Fx}{lA}$

The strain energy density (energy per unit volume) is

$\dfrac{dU}{dV} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\sigma2}{Y} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{F^{2}x^{2}}{YA^{2}l^{2}}$, where $dV = Adx$ is the volume of a small part of the rod

So the energy stored in the rod is

$U = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{F2}{YA^{2}l^{2}}{∫}_{0}^{l}x^{2}dx$

$U = \dfrac{F^{2}l}{6A^{2}Y}$

questions.q: A particular force $F$ applied on a wire increases its length by $2 \times {10}^{- 3}m$. If we were to increase the wire's length by $4 \times {10}^{- 3}m$, then the applied force is $nF$. What is the value of $n$?
questions.solution:
$Y = \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{l}{L}} = \dfrac{F \times L}{A \times l}$ [$l$ = Change in length, $L$ = Original length] (where $Y$ is Young's modulus of elasticity)

Since $Y$, $L$ and $A$ remain same.
$⇒ F ∝ l$
$⇒ \dfrac{{F}_{1}}{{F}_{2}} = \dfrac{{l}_{1}}{{l}_{2}}$
$⇒ \dfrac{F}{{F}_{2}} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 3}}{4 \times {10}^{- 3}}$

$⇒ {F}_{2} = 2F ⇒ {F}_{2} = nF ⇒ n = 2$

questions.q: One of the square faces of a metal slab of side $50$ cm and thickness $20$ cm is rigidly fixed on a horizontal surface. If a tangential force of $30N$ is applied to the top face and it is known that the shear modulus of the material is $4 \times {10}^{10}N / m^{2}$, then the displacement (in $m$) of the top face is
questions.solution:
Shear strain, $ε = tan ⁡ \theta = \theta = \dfrac{x}{l}$

$η = \dfrac{σ}{ε}$

Or $x = \dfrac{F ⋅ l}{A ⋅ η}$

Given $F = 30N$

$A = 50 \times 50 \times {10}^{- 4}$

$η = 4 \times {10}^{10}$

$x = \dfrac{30 \times 20 \times {10}^{- 2}}{50 \times 50 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 4 \times {10}^{10}}$

$= \dfrac{6}{25 \times 4 \times {10}^{- 2} \times {10}^{10}}$

$= 6 \times {10}^{- 10}m$

questions.q: Two wires of the same material (Young's modulus $Y$) and same length $L$ but radii $R$ and $2R$ respectively are joined end to end and a weight $w$ is suspended from the combination as shown in the figure. The elastic potential energy in the system is
questions.solution:
${k}_{1} = \dfrac{Y \pi{\left(2R\right)}^{2}}{L}$, ${k}_{2} = \dfrac{Y \pi{\left(R\right)}^{2}}{L}$

Equivalent $\dfrac{1}{{k}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{k}_{2}} = \dfrac{L}{4{Y \pi R}^{2}} + \dfrac{L}{{Y \pi R}^{2}}$

Since, ${k}_{1}{x}_{1} = {k}_{2}{x}_{2} = w$

Elastic potential energy of the system

$U ⁡ = \dfrac{1}{2}{k}_{1}{x}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{k}_{2}{x}_{2}^{2}$

$U = \dfrac{1}{2}{k}_{1}{\left(\dfrac{w}{{k}_{1}}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{k}_{2}{\left(\dfrac{w}{{k}_{2}}\right)}^{2}$

   $= \dfrac{1}{2}{w}^{2}\left\{\dfrac{1}{{k}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{k}_{2}}\right\} = \dfrac{1}{2}{w}^{2}\left(\dfrac{5L}{4{Y \pi R}^{2}}\right)$

$U ⁡ = \dfrac{5{w}^{2}L}{8{\pi YR}^{2}}$

questions.q:
A thin rod of negligible mass and area of cross-section $4 \times {10}^{- 6}{m}^{2}$, suspended vertically from one end, has a length of $\text{0.5}m$ at $100 ° C$. The rod is cooled to $0 ° C$ but prevented from contracting by attaching a mass at the lower end. The value of this mass is
(Given, coefficient of linear expansion is ${10}^{- 5} ° {C}^{- 1}$, Young's modulus is $Y = {10}^{11}N{m}^{- 2}$ and $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
The change in length due to decrease in temperature,

$\Delta {\text{l}}_{1} = \text{L}\alpha \Delta \theta = \left(0 \cdot 5\right)\left({10}^{- 5}\right)\left(0 - 100\right)$

$\Delta {\text{l}}_{1} = - 0 \cdot 5 \times {10}^{- 3}\text{m}$ ... (i)

Negative sign implies that length is decreasing. Now let $M$ be the mass attached to the lower end. Then, change in length due to suspension of load is

$\Delta {\text{l}}_{2} = \dfrac{\left(\text{Mg}\right)\text{L}}{\text{AY}} = \dfrac{\left(\text{M}\right)\left(10\right)\left(\text{0.5}\right)}{\left(4 \times {10}^{- 6}\right)\left({10}^{11}\right)}$

$\Delta {\text{l}}_{2} = \left(\text{1.25} \times {10}^{- 5}\right)M$ ... (ii)

$\Delta {\text{l}}_{1} + \Delta {\text{l}}_{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\text{1.25} \times {10}^{- 5}\right)M = \left(\text{0.5} \times {10}^{- 3}\right)$ (from equations (i) and (ii))

$⇒ M = \dfrac{\text{0.5} \times {10}^{- 3}}{\text{1.25} \times {10}^{- 5}}kg$

$⇒ M = 40kg$

questions.q: The elastic limit of brass is $379$ MPa. The minimum diameter of a brass rod if it is to support a $400N$ load without exceeding its elastic limit will be
questions.solution:
Stress $= \dfrac{F}{A}$
Elastic limit is $379$ MPa
$⇒ 379 \times {10}^{6} = \dfrac{400}{A} = \dfrac{400}{\pid^{2} / 4}$
$d = \sqrt{\dfrac{400 \times 4}{\pi \times 379 \times {10}^{6}}}$
$= 1.16 \times {10}^{- 3}m$
$= 1.16mm$

questions.q: A heavy plank of mass $100$ kg hangs on three vertical wires of equal length arranged symmetrically (see figure). All the wires have the same cross-section. The middle wire is of steel and the other two are of copper. The modulus of elasticity of steel is assumed to be double that of copper. Determine the tensions in the wire. ( use $g = 9. 8ms^{- 2}$& )
questions.solution:
Let tension in copper and steel wires are& ${T}_{cu}$ and ${T}_{st}$. Assuming same strain (due to heavy plank) we note that

${Y}_{steel} = \dfrac{T{⁡}_{st}L ⁡}{A ⁡ \left(\Delta L ⁡\right)}$ and&

or& $\dfrac{T{⁡}_{st}}{T{⁡}_{cu}} = \dfrac{Y{⁡}_{steel}}{Y{⁡}_{cu}} = 2 \left(\text{given}\right)or $ T{⁡}_{st} = 2T{⁡}_{cu}$

Further, ${T}_{st} + 2{T}_{cu} = 100kg ( given )$



or2{T}_{cu} + 2{T}_{cu} = 100kg$ or ${T}_{cu} = 25kg$

And therefore, ${T}_{st} = 2{T}_{cu} = 50kg$

Thus ${T}_{cu}$ is & ${T}_{cu} = 25kgf = 245N$

and& ${T}_{st} = 50kgf = 490N$

questions.q: Two blocks of masses $5$ kg and $10$ kg are connected by a metal wire going over a smooth pulley as shown in the figure. The breaking stress of the metal wire is $2 \times {10}^{9}Nm^{- 2}$. If $g = 10ms^{- 2}$,& then what is the minimum radius of the wire which will not break
questions.solution:
This is Atwood's machine. Let the tension in the wire be $T$ and acceleration of masses $a$.

Then, $T - 5g = 5a$ and $10g - T = 10a$

This gives $a = \dfrac{1}{3}g$ and $T ⁡ = \dfrac{20}{3}\text{g} = \dfrac{200}{3}\text{N}$.

Stress $= \dfrac{T ⁡}{area} = \dfrac{200}{3 \times 3\text{.}14 \times r{⁡}^{2}} = 2 \times {10}^{9}\text{(given)}$

Thus the minimum radius $r$ should be $r = \sqrt{\dfrac{200}{3 \times 3\text{.}14 \times 2 \times {10}^{9}}} = 1\text{.}03 \times {10}^{- 4}m \approx 0\text{.}1\text{mm}$

questions.q: A bottle has an opening of radius $a$ and length $b$. A cork of length $b$ and radius $\left(a + ∆ a\right)$~where& $\left(∆ a ≪ a\right)$, is compressed to fit into the opening completely (see figure). If the bulk modulus of cork is $B$ and the coefficient of friction between the bottle and cork is $\mu$, then the force needed to push the cork into the bottle is
questions.solution:
$Pressure = \dfrac{N}{A} = \dfrac{N}{\left(2\pi a\right)b}$

$⇒ stress = B \times strain$

$\dfrac{N}{\left(2\pi a\right)b} = B\dfrac{2\pi a ∆ a \times b}{{\pia}^{2}b}$

$⇒ N = B$

$f = \mu N = \mu4\pi bB \Delta a$

questions.q: A wire suspended vertically from one of its ends is stretched by attaching a weight of $200N$ to the lower end. The weight stretches the wire by $1$ mm. Then the elastic energy stored in the wire is
questions.solution:
Elastic energy per unit volume = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain}$

$∴$ Elastic energy = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain} \times \text{volume} $

= $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{F}{A} \times \dfrac{\Delta \text{L}}{L} \times \left(\text{AL}\right)

$= $\dfrac{1}{2}\text{F} \Delta \text{L} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{200} \times {10}^{- 3}\text{=0.1 J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The longitudinal stress in a rod (with rectangular cross-section) is $1 %$ of the Young's modulus of its material. What is the approximate percentage of change of its volume? (Poisson's ratio of the material of the rod is $0. 3$)
questions.solution:
$∵$ Stress, $\dfrac{F}{∆ A} = 1%$ of $Y = \dfrac{Y}{100}$ But $Young′s$ modulus, $Y = \dfrac{stress}{strain} = \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{∆ A}}{\dfrac{∆ l}{l}}$

$∴ Y = \dfrac{\dfrac{Y}{100}}{\dfrac{∆ l}{l}} \left($ putting$\dfrac{F}{∆ A} = \dfrac{Y}{100}\right)

$∴ $\dfrac{∆ l}{l} = \dfrac{1}{100}

${Poisson}^{′}s$ ratio, \sigma = \dfrac{- \dfrac{∆ r}{r}}{\dfrac{∆ l}{l}}

$∴ $\dfrac{∆ r}{r} = - \sigma$⋅ $\dfrac{∆ l}{l} = \dfrac{- 0.3}{100}

\dfrac{∆ r}{r} = \dfrac{- 0.3}{100}

$∴$ Change in volume, \dfrac{∆ V}{V} = \dfrac{2 ∆ r}{r} + \dfrac{∆ l}{l}

$= $\dfrac{2 \times \left(- 0.3\right)}{100} + \dfrac{1}{100}

$= $\dfrac{1 - 0.6}{100} = \dfrac{0.4}{100}

So the percentage change in volume = 0.4%$

questions.q: A sphere of radius $0. 1m$ and mass $8 \pi \text{kg}$ is attached to the lower end of a steel wire of length $5. 0m$ & diameter ${10}^{- 3}m$. The wire is suspended from $5. 22m$ high ceiling of a room. When the sphere is made to swing like a simple pendulum, it just grazes the floor at its lowest point. Calculate the velocity of the sphere at the lowest position. $Y$ for steel = $1. 994 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$
questions.solution:
As the length of the wire is $5m$ and diameter $2 \times 0 . 1 = 0 . 2m$ and at the lowest point, it grazes the floor which is at a distance $5 . 22m$ from the roof, the increase in the length of the wire at lowest point



$\Delta \text{L} = 5 \text{.} 2 2 - \left(5 + 0 \text{.}2\right)$

$= 0 \text{.}0 2 \text{m}$

So the tension in the wire (due to elasticity)

$T = \dfrac{YA}{L} \Delta$ L = $\dfrac{1\text{.}994 \times 1{0}^{11} \times \pi\left(5 \times 1{0}^{- 4}\right)2 \times 0\text{.}02}{5} ==199\text{.}}4\pi\text{$ N}

and as the equation of circular - motion of a mass $m$ tied to a string in a vertical plane is

$\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} =$ T - m$\text{g cos}$\theta$

So at the lowest point

\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} =$ T - m$\text{g} \left[\text{as} \theta = 0\right]$

But here $r = 5 + 0 . 02 + 0 . 1 = 5 . 12m$

So $\left(\dfrac{8\piv^{2}}{5 . 12}\right) = 199\text{.}4\pi - 8\pi \times 9\text{.}8$

i.e., $v^{2} = \left(1 2 1 \times 5 \text{.} 1 2 / 8\right) = 7 7 \text{.} 4 4$

So $v = 8 . 8ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: One end of a long metallic wire of length $L$ is tied to the ceiling. The other end is tied to a massless spring of spring constant $k$. A mass $m$ hangs freely from the free end of the spring. The area of cross-section and Young’s modulus of the wire are $A$ and $Y$ respectively. If the mass is slightly pulled down and released, it will oscillate with a time period $T$ equal to&
options:
$2\pi\left(\dfrac{m}{k}\right)^{1} / 2$
&

$2\pi \left[ \left(\dfrac{mYA}{kL}$\right)$\dfrac{1}{2}$\right]
&
questions.solution:
Equivalent force constant for a wire is given by $k = \dfrac{YA}{L}$. Because in case of a wire, $F = \dfrac{YA}{L} ∆ L$ and in case of spring, $F = k ∆ x$. Comparing these two, we find k of wire $= \dfrac{YA}{L}$

${k}_{eq} = \dfrac{{k}_{1}{k}_{2}}{{k}_{1} + {k}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{YA}{L}k}{\dfrac{YA}{L} + k} = \dfrac{YAk}{YA + Lk}$



$∴ T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k\text{eq}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m\left(YA + Lk\right)}{YAk}}$
&

questions.q: A rigid bar of mass $15$ kg is supported symmetrically by three wires, each of length $2m$. The wires at the endpoints are made of copper and the middle& one is made of steel. If the tension in each wire is the same, then the ratio of the diameter of copper wire to the diameter of steel wire is [Given, ${Y}_{copper} = 1. 1 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$ and ${Y}_{steel} = 1. 9 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$]
questions.solution:
Young's modulus of copper $( {Y}_{1} ) = 1 . 1 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$

Young's modulus of steel $( {Y}_{2} ) = 1 . 9 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$

Let ${d}_{1}$ and ${d}_{2}$ be the diameters of copper and steel wires respectively.

Since the tension is the same in each wire, therefore each wire has the same extension. Also, as each wire is of the same length, the strain in each of them is the same.

$Y = \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{∆ l}{l}}$

$\dfrac{Y1}{Y2} = \left(\dfrac{d2}{d1}\right)2$

$\dfrac{d1}{d2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{Y2}{Y1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{19}{11}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The pressure applied from all directions on a cube is $p.$ How much its temperature should be raised to maintain the original volume? The volume elasticity of the cube is $\beta$ and the coefficient of volume expansion is $\alpha.$
questions.solution:
If coefficient of volume expansion is $\alpha$ and rise in temperature is $∆ \theta,$ then $∆ V = V\alpha ∆ \theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{∆ V}{V} = \alpha ∆ \theta$

$∴$ Volume elasticity, $\beta = \dfrac{p}{∆ V / V}$

$= \dfrac{p}{\alpha ∆ \theta}$

$⇒ ∆ \theta = \dfrac{p}{\alpha\beta}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The length of a metal wire is ${l}_{1}$ when the tension in it is ${T}_{1}$ and is ${l}_{2}$ when the tension is ${T}_{2}$. The natural length of wire is
questions.solution:
Let the original length be $l$.

In first case,

${l}_{1} = l + d{l}_{1}$

Using Hooke's law, $x = \dfrac{T}{K}$

Where, $x$ is the displacement.

We have, ${l}_{1} = l + \dfrac{{T}_{1}}{K}$... (i)

Similarly, ${l}_{2} = l + \dfrac{{T}_{2}}{K}$... (ii)

Solving Equations. (i) and (ii), we get

$l = \dfrac{{l}_{1}{T}_{2} - {l}_{2}{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2} - {T}_{1}}$

The strain produced in the wire, (if the vertical distance through which the midpoint of the wire moves down $x < l$) will be
questions.solution:
From figure the increase in length $∆ l = \left(PR + RQ\right) - PQ$

= 2PR – PQ

$= 2{\left(l^{2} + x^{2}\right)}^{1 / 2} - 2l = 2l{\left(1 + \dfrac{x^{2}}{l^{2}}\right)}^{1 / 2} - 2l$

$= 2l\left[1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{x^{2}}{l^{2}}\right] - 2l$ ( By Binomial theorem)

$= x^{2} / l$

$∴ Strain = ∆ l / 2l = x^{2} / 2l^{2}$

Calculate the change in temperature of the wire if $75 %$ of the stored elastic potential energy is converted into heat. &

questions.solution:
As work done in stretching an elastic body per unit volume is given by

& & & $\dfrac{\text{W}}{\text{V}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{stress} \times \text{strain} = \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{{stress}^{2}}{\text{Y}} \left[\text{as Y} = \dfrac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain} \text{ and } }\right] ........ (1)

So \text{W} = \dfrac{1}{2} {\left[\dfrac{\text{Mg}}{\text{A}}\right]}^{2} \dfrac{\text{V}}{\text{Y}} \left[\text{as stress} = \dfrac{\text{F}}{\text{A}} = \dfrac{\text{Mg}}{\text{A}}\right]

Now according to given problem heat produced H = (75/100) W $= $\dfrac{3}{4} . \text{W}

$⇒$ \text{ms} \Delta \theta = \dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{2} {\left[\dfrac{\text{Mg}}{\pi r^{2}}\right]}^{2} \dfrac{\text{V}}{\text{Y}} \left[\text{as H} = \text{ms} \Delta \theta\right]using equation (1)

or \left($ρ $\text{V}\right) \text{s} \Delta \theta = \dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{2} { \left[\dfrac{\text{Mg}}{\pi r^{2}}\right]}^{2}\dfrac{\text{V}}{\text{Y}}\left[\text{as m} =$ρ $\text{V}\right]

$∴ $\Delta \theta = \dfrac{3}{8} {\left[\dfrac{3 1 \text{.} 4 \times 9 \text{.} 8}{\pi \times 1 {0}^{- 6}}\right]}^{2} \dfrac{1}{9 \text{.} 8 \times 1 {0}^{1 0}} \times \dfrac{1}{9 \times 1 {0}^{3} \times 4 9 0}

i.e., \Delta \theta = \dfrac{1}{1 2 0} \text{K} =8 \text{.}3 3 \times1 {0}^{- 3} \text{K}$

questions.q: $32g$ of ${O}_{2}_{}is contained in a cubical container of side 1m$ and maintained at a temperature of $127 ° C$. The isothermal bulk modulus of elasticity of the gas is (universal gas constant=$R$)
options:
$127R$
&

$400R$
&

$200R$
&

$560R$
&
questions.solution:
The bulk modulus of elasticity at a constant temperature

$PV = nRT$

$\dfrac{dP}{P} = \dfrac{dV}{V}$

$B = - \dfrac{dP}{dV / V}$

$B = P$

$B = \dfrac{nRT}{V} = \dfrac{R\left(400\right)}{{1}^{3}} = 400R$

The change of temperature required to produce the same elongation, if the steel rod is heated, is (The modulus of elasticity is $3 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$ and the coefficient of linear expansion of steel is $1.1 \times {10}^{- 5}{℃}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
Modulus of elasticity =$\dfrac{Force}{Area} \times \dfrac{l}{∆ l}$

$3 \times {10}^{11} = \dfrac{33000}{{10}^{- 3}} \times \dfrac{l}{∆ l}$

$\dfrac{∆ l}{l} = \dfrac{33000}{{10}^{- 3}} \times \dfrac{1}{3 \times {10}^{11}}$

$= 11 \times {10}^{- 5}$

Change in length, $\dfrac{∆ l}{l} = \alpha ∆ T$

$11 \times {10}^{- 5}$ = $1.1 \times {10}^{- 5} \times ∆ T$

$⇒∆ T = 10K$ or& $10 ° C$

questions.solution: Given, diameter of wires (2r)=0.25 cm r=0.125 cm=1.25 × 10^{-3} m For steel wire, Load (F_{1})=(4 + 6) kgf=10 × 9.8 N=98 N Length of steel wire (l_{1})=1.5 m Young's modulus (Y_{1})=2.0 × 10^{11} Pa $\text{Young's modulus (Y)}=\dfrac{{F}_{1} \times {l ⁡}_{1}}{{A}_{1} \times \text{\Delta} {l ⁡}_{1}} \text{Change in length} \left(\text{\Delta} {l ⁡}_{1}\right)=\dfrac{{F}_{1} \times {l ⁡}_{1}}{{A}_{1} \times {Y}_{1}} =\dfrac{{F}_{1} \times {l ⁡}_{1}}{\text{\pi} {r}_{1}^{2} \times {Y}_{1}} =\dfrac{\text{98} \times \text{1.5}}{\text{3.14} \times {\left(\text{1.25} \times {10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2} \times \text{2.0} \times {10}^{11}}$ =1.5 × 10^{-4} m For brass wire, Load (F_{2})=6 kgf=6 × 9.8 N=58.8 N Length of brass wire (l_{2})=1.0 m Young's modulus (Y_{2})=0.91 × 10^{11} Pa $\text{Change in length} \left({l ⁡}_{2}\right)=\dfrac{{F}_{2} \times {l ⁡}_{2}}{\text{\pi} {r}_{2}^{2} \times {Y}_{2}} =\dfrac{\text{58.8} \times \text{1.0}}{\text{3.14} \times {\left(\text{1.25} \times {10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2} \times \text{0.91} \times {10}^{11}}$ =1.3 × 10^{-4} m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An open cylindrical vessel filled with water is rotated together with water at angular speed $1rad{s}^{- 1}$. At this angular speed, the centre of the bottom is just exposed. If the angular speed is increased to $\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}rad{s}^{- 1}$, how much area (in ${cm}^{2}$) of the bottom of the vessel is now exposed to surrounding? [Area of the cross-section of cylinder is $27{cm}^{2}$]
questions.solution:
Let ${\omega}_{1}$ be initial angular velocity

$\dfrac{{{\omega}_{1}}^{2}{R}^{2}}{2g} = h$
For angular velocity ${\omega}_{2}$ let radius of exposed surface be x

$\dfrac{{{\omega}_{2}}^{2}}{2g}\left[{R}^{2} - {x}^{2}\right] = h$
Putting the value of ${\omega}_{1}$ and ${\omega}_{2}$
$\pi{x}^{2} = 9$
Since $\pi{R}^{2} = 27$

questions.q: A sphere of radius $0. 1m$ and mass $8 \pi \text{kg}$ is attached to the lower end of a steel wire of length $5. 0m$ & diameter ${10}^{- 3}m$. The wire is suspended from $5. 22m$ high ceiling of a room. When the sphere is made to swing like a simple pendulum, it just grazes the floor at its lowest point. Calculate the velocity of the sphere at the lowest position. $Y$ for steel = $1. 994 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$
questions.solution:
As the length of the wire is $5m$ and diameter $2 \times 0 . 1 = 0 . 2m$ and at the lowest point, it grazes the floor which is at a distance $5 . 22m$ from the roof, the increase in the length of the wire at lowest point



$\Delta \text{L} = 5 \text{.} 2 2 - \left(5 + 0 \text{.}2\right)$

$= 0 \text{.}0 2 \text{m}$

So the tension in the wire (due to elasticity)

$T = \dfrac{YA}{L} \Delta$ L = $\dfrac{1\text{.}994 \times 1{0}^{11} \times \pi\left(5 \times 1{0}^{- 4}\right)2 \times 0\text{.}02}{5} ==199\text{.}}4\pi\text{$ N}

and as the equation of circular - motion of a mass $m$ tied to a string in a vertical plane is

$\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} =$ T - m$\text{g cos}$\theta$

So at the lowest point

\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} =$ T - m$\text{g} \left[\text{as} \theta = 0\right]$

But here $r = 5 + 0 . 02 + 0 . 1 = 5 . 12m$

So $\left(\dfrac{8\piv^{2}}{5 . 12}\right) = 199\text{.}4\pi - 8\pi \times 9\text{.}8$

i.e., $v^{2} = \left(1 2 1 \times 5 \text{.} 1 2 / 8\right) = 7 7 \text{.} 4 4$

So $v = 8 . 8ms^{- 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The edge of an aluminium cube is $10$ cm long. One face of the cube is firmly fixed to a vertical wall. A mass of $100$ kg is then attached to the opposite face of the cube. The shear modulus of aluminium is $25$ GPa. What is the vertical deflection of this face?
options:
$3. 92 \times {10}^{- 7}m$
&
questions.solution:
Given, side of a cube (l) = 10 cm & = 0.1 m

Area its each face (A) = l^{2} = (0.1)^{2} = 0.01 m^{2}

Load (m) = 100 kg

Tangential force acting on one face of the cube,

F = mg = 100 × 9.8 = 980 N

$\text{Shear stress acting on this face} = \dfrac{\text{F}}{\text{A}}$

$= \dfrac{\text{980}}{\text{0.01}} {N/m}^{2}$

= 9.8 × 10^{4} N/m^{2}

Shear modulus of aluminium (η)) = 25 GPa

= 25 × 10^{9} N/m^{2}

$\text{Shear modulus} \left(η\right) = \dfrac{\text{Shearing stress}}{\text{Shearing strain}}$

$\text{or shearing strain} \left(\dfrac{\text{\Delta} \text{y}}{\text{L}}\right) = \dfrac{\text{Shearing stress}}{\text{Shear modulus}}$

$\text{or} \text{\Delta} \text{y} = \dfrac{\text{Shearing stress}}{\text{Shear modulus}} \times \text{L}$

$= \dfrac{\text{9.8} \times {10}^{4}}{\text{25} \times {10}^{9}} \times \text{0.1}$

= 0.392 × 10^{-5} m

= 3.92 × 10^{-7} m
